tool_arguments.query: Microsoft FY2025 Q2 data center capital expenditure FY2025 Q2 earnings

events.content: Microsoft FY2025 Q2 data center capital expenditure FY2025 Q2 earnings

Microsoft’s FY2025 Q3 (quarter ended March 31, 2025) capital expenditures, **including finance leases**, were **$21.4 billion**, while cash paid for property, plant, and equipment was **$16.7 billion**. [[1]] 
The roughly **$4.7 billion** difference reflects the quarter’s finance-lease component, principally related to data-center capacity timing. [[1]] 
Management said approximately **half** of cloud- and AI-related spending went to long-lived assets expected to support monetization for **15 years or more**; the other half was primarily CPUs and GPUs used to meet demand signals, including a **$315 billion** contracted backlog. [[1]] 
This was a substantial step-up from FY2024 Q3’s **$14.0 billion** of capex including finance leases—an increase of approximately **53% year over year**—while cash PP&E spending rose from **$11.0 billion** to **$16.7 billion**. [[2]] [[1]] 
Microsoft attributed the Q3 FY2025 amount being slightly below its expectations to normal variability in the timing of data-center lease deliveries, not a reduction in AI infrastructure commitment. [[1]] 
For FY2025 Q4, the company guided that capex would rise sequentially, while maintaining its prior aggregate second-half FY2025 capex outlook. [[1]] 
Management also said AI demand was growing faster than capacity additions and expected some AI capacity constraints to persist beyond June 2025. [[1]] 
For FY2026, Microsoft expected capex to keep growing but at a lower rate than FY2025, with a greater proportion of shorter-lived assets tied more directly to revenue. [[1]]

[S1.2] Microsoft (MSFT) Q3 2024 Earnings Call Transcript — https://www.fool.com/earnings/call-transcripts/2024/04/25/microsoft-msft-q3-2024-earnings-call-transcript/

tool_arguments.query: Alphabet FY2025 Q2 data center capital expenditure earnings

events.content: Alphabet FY2025 Q2 data center capital expenditure earnings

**Alphabet’s Q3 FY2025 AI-infrastructure spending accelerated sharply:** reported capital expenditure was **$24.0 billion** for the quarter ended September 30, 2025, versus **$13.0 billion** in Q3 2024—an increase of approximately **85% year over year**. [[1, 2]]

- The “vast majority” of Q3 capex went to **technical infrastructure**, with roughly **60% ($14.4 billion)** directed to **servers** and **40% ($9.6 billion)** to **data-center and networking equipment**. [[1]]
- Alphabet’s 10-Q defines technical infrastructure as servers and network equipment supporting computing, storage, networking—including AI—and data-center land and building construction; therefore, the $24 billion is best viewed as AI-enabled infrastructure spending rather than a company-disclosed, AI-only capex figure. [[3]]
- Google Cloud’s Q3 revenue rose **34% to $15.2 billion**, with growth driven in part by enterprise AI infrastructure and AI solutions, while Cloud backlog increased by **$49 billion sequentially**. [[1]]
- Management said supply would remain tight in Q4 2025 and 2026 despite faster server deployments and data-center construction, underpinning continued aggressive capacity investment. [[1]]

**FY2025 outlook:** Alphabet raised expected full-year capex to **$91–$93 billion**, from its prior **$85 billion** outlook. [[1]] Through the first nine months of 2025, purchases of property and equipment were **$63.596 billion**, compared with **$38.259 billion** in the comparable 2024 period. [[3]]

**Profit-and-cash-flow implications:** Q3 depreciation rose **$1.6 billion year over year to $5.6 billion**, or **41%**, and Alphabet expected depreciation growth to accelerate modestly in Q4 as the enlarged infrastructure base enters service. [[1]] Management also indicated that 2026 capex would increase significantly, with specifics to follow at its Q4 results. [[1]]

Sources:
[S3.1] Alphabet Investor Relations - 2025 Q3 Earnings Call — https://abc.xyz/investor/events/event-details/2025/2025-Q3-Earnings-Call-2025-4OI4Bac_Q9/default.aspx

- **Alphabet (Q2 2026, ended June 30):** Google advertising revenue was **$81.629 billion**, up **14% year over year** from $71.340 billion; it comprised **$63.271 billion** of Google Search & Other, **$11.055 billion** of YouTube ads, and **$7.303 billion** of Google Network revenue. [[1]]
- **Meta (Q2 2026, ended June 30):** advertising revenue was **$59.363 billion**, up **27% year over year** from $46.563 billion. [[2]]
- Alphabet’s quarterly advertising revenue was therefore about **$22.266 billion higher** than Meta’s, although Meta delivered the faster year-over-year growth rate. [[1, 2]]

private_messages.content:
“Sales” are not directly comparable across these four products because the companies disclose different measures—platform/segment revenue, installed devices, or third-party shipment estimates rather than product-specific sales. [[1, 2]]

| Product | Best disclosed sales indicator | What it does—and does not—measure |
|---|---:|---|
| **Microsoft Xbox** | **$23.455bn FY2025 Gaming revenue**, up 9% year over year; Xbox hardware revenue fell 25%. [[1]]| This is the entire Gaming business—Xbox hardware, first- and third-party content, Game Pass, cloud gaming, advertising and other cloud services—not console sales alone. [[1]] Microsoft does not provide current console-unit sales in the annual-report disclosure cited here. [[1]]|
| **Google Pixel** | Alphabet’s **Subscriptions, Platforms and Devices** revenue was **$48.03bn in FY2025**, versus $40.34bn in FY2024. [[3]]| This category includes subscriptions and platforms as well as devices, so it is **not Pixel revenue**. [[4]] Alphabet does not separately disclose Pixel units or Pixel revenue; a third-party-derived estimate puts 2025 Pixel shipments at roughly **15m units**, but that is not company-reported. [[5]]|
| **Amazon Alexa** | Amazon said there were **more than 600m Alexa devices** in use as of February 26, 2025. [[6]]| This is an installed/device base across Alexa-enabled products, not annual Echo-unit sales or Alexa revenue. [[6]] Amazon does not provide a separately reported Alexa hardware or service-revenue line in the material retrieved. [[6]]|
| **Meta Quest** | Meta’s **Reality Labs FY2025 revenue was $2.207bn** and its operating loss was **$19.193bn**. [[7, 8]]| Reality Labs includes virtual-, augmented- and mixed-reality consumer hardware, software and content, so the revenue is **not Quest-only**. [[2]] Meta does not publicly disclose Quest unit sales; IDC data reported by Forbes estimates **1.7m Quest shipments in the first three quarters of 2025**, down 16% year over year. [[9]]|

**Bottom line:** Xbox is the only one of the four with a large, directly reported product-ecosystem revenue figure; Pixel and Quest must be assessed through broad reporting categories plus external shipment estimates; Alexa’s most meaningful disclosed figure is its 600m-plus device footprint rather than sales revenue. [[1, 3, 6, 7]]
